A_general.open_code_note: No official public server repository or package was found in the collected evidence.
A_general.mcp_protocol_version: 2025-03-26 revision and above (official developer documentation); Support overview also refers to the Authorization standards published November 11, 2025.
other_official_servers: The Support overview discusses Outreach as an MCP Client connecting to third-party MCP servers; it is a separate product role, not another endpoint for this server.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Requires the Outreach Amplify add-on with active credits, an active licensed Outreach seat, and Amplify enabled for the organization. Exact MCP pricing is not published; Outreach directs customers to their pricing guidance or partner.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Outreach plan and Amplify add-on pricing are not published in the consulted official material.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: API throttle limits apply. The number of MCP calls generated by a user query depends on the agent and is nondeterministic; each tool call counts as an API call to the endpoint.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: An organization admin must enable the server. Optional organization settings control create actions (on by default) and delete actions (off by default). User must be active, licensed, authenticated, and permitted by their Outreach profile. Client-auth-only authentication is not supported.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Outreach organization admin controls server enablement and create/delete settings; Outreach user profile and identity provider control user access; Outreach controls API throttling.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: Remote tools are discovered through tools/list. The developer catalog lists 42 tools: 27 read/discovery, 13 write/mutation, and 2 schema tools. Support documentation describes the tool families and representative parameters.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Official response documentation describes structured JSON objects: search results as {count, <resource>: [...]}, get-by-ID as {<resource>: {...}}, create as {<resource>: {id, ...}}, delete as {id: "<deleted_id>"}, batch operations as {batch: {state, total, failures, ...}}, and schema results as field arrays.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Bearer token in the Authorization header. The endpoint returned HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://api.outreach.io/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource" and body {"error":"No Authorization header.","description":"You must provide an Authorization header with a valid access token."}. Protected-resource metadata: resource https://api.outreach.io/mcp; authorization_servers [https://api.outreach.io]; scopes_supported [prospects.all]; bearer_methods_supported [header]. Authorization-server metadata: issuer https://api.outreach.io; authorization_endpoint https://api.outreach.io/mcpOAuth/authorize; token_endpoint https://api.outreach.io/mcpOAuth/token; registration_endpoint https://api.outreach.io/mcpOAuth/register; scopes_supported [prospects.all]; response_types_supported [code]; grant_types_supported [authorization_code, refresh_token]; token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported [client_secret_post]; code_challenge_methods_supported [S256]. OpenID configuration returned HTTP 404 route not found. Token lifetime and token revocation details are not stated in the supplied metadata; docs say revocation is IDP-controlled.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: OAuth 2.1 authorization code with PKCE and Dynamic Client Registration. The endpoint requires a bearer token in the Authorization header. Product permissions inherit from the authenticated Outreach user's RBAC profile. Supplied metadata advertises the scope prospects.all, authorization code and refresh token grants, S256 PKCE, and client_secret_post token authentication. Docs say IDP controls revocation; metadata provides no token lifetime.

C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Unauthenticated endpoint request returned HTTP 401 and the stated missing-Authorization error.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official catalog: 27 read/discovery tools are annotated readOnlyHint:true, destructiveHint:false, idempotentHint:true. Write tools have readOnlyHint:false and idempotentHint:false; deletes and sequence removal have destructiveHint:true. Catalog says openWorldHint:false for all tools, while the annotation explainer says all tools have openWorldHint:true. 2. Deletes require explicit user confirmation according to Support docs; tool annotations are client hints, not a server-enforced confirmation gate. No enforced confirmation parameter or elicitation flow found. 3. OAuth metadata advertises prospects.all. Docs say user RBAC permissions apply on every call; server requires active licensed user and organization Amplify. Admin enables server; create setting defaults on, delete setting defaults off. DCR is available; docs suggest IDP controls to restrict clients. Docs say IDP controls revocation; token lifetime not found. 4. Organization-level create/delete settings and per-tool client permissions are documented. No read-only endpoint, URL toolset filter, or query-free mode found. Support docs mention production/non-production instances; no region list found. 5. Data access follows user profile permissions; meeting visibility follows authorized profile permissions. No field masking or PII exclusion rules found. 6. API throttle limits apply; exact thresholds not published. Sequence meeting fetch can return up to 50 per call. Batch tools return batch status. No MCP-specific price per call documented. 7. Schemas expose required fields and constraints at runtime; custom fields and valid filters are discoverable. Runtime unknown-argument handling, coercion, and parameter correction are not documented. Support docs state sequence_create defaults owner to current user and throttle to 50/day. 8. Auth docs say calls are attributed to authenticated user in activity history. Client logging is recommended; server telemetry and retention details not found. 9. The official 42-tool list has no feedback/rating/report/survey tools. Catalog describes account_answer_question and opportunity_answer_question as creating Q&A records; no upsell result or marketing instruction found. 10. No server-delivered skills found. Official developer best practices recommend runtime schema discovery, confirmations for destructive operations, audit logging, and batching. These recommendations are client guidance. 11. No cross-session memory or behavior-dependent tool changes documented. 12. Flat list of 42 tools is documented; no proxy or sub-server hierarchy found. 13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or equivalent escape hatch found in official tool list.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Let the agent discover schemas at runtime via tools/list; don't hardcode field lists
Honor MCP annotation hints — confirm on destructiveHint: true, auto-approve readOnlyHint: true
Chain tools to compose workflows; don't reach for REST when MCP can handle it
Add user confirmation before destructive operations (delete, sequence removal)
Log every tool call for audit
Build polling loops on batch tools; check state once and use webhooks for long-running ops
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: Official developer catalog presents one flat tool list. No proxying, nested server, or dynamic toolset architecture is documented.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official developer Tool Catalog lists 42 tools (27 read/discovery, 13 write/mutation, 2 schema); the official Support overview names the same operations in prose. The official docs landing page still says 32 tools, contradicting the current Tool Catalog count. actions.json includes all 42 official names and 14 additional names from the Claude connector directory. Claude's directory is a third-party listing even though it labels the connector Anthropic verified; its names differ from the official tool names and are retained as catalogue-only entries. Other catalogue reports: apis.io says 41 tools (27 read, 11 write, 3 schema); mcp.so has no tool list; MCPmetrics shows no tool count; mcpforgtm summarizes capabilities without an exact count; Obot lists capability summaries but no exact count. The 14 catalogue names are not assumed to be aliases of the official names.

E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Support documentation states MCP does not edit/update existing records; it offers read, create, and delete operations. The MCP tool catalog provides no update tool. Other Outreach product/API functions may exist outside MCP, but this research did not enumerate the full REST API. Sources: https://support.outreach.io/support/solutions/articles/159000425158-outreach-mcp-server-overview and https://developers.outreach.io/mcp-server/tool-catalog

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Official guidance asks clients to add confirmation before destructive operations, honor destructiveHint, log calls, and avoid tight write loops. The usage guide states: "Writes are real. Build in confirmation flows, audit logging, and rate limits in your agent layer. The MCP server does not throttle or undo." The server catalog marks destructive tools, but client confirmation remains a client behavior.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Authentication documentation says permissions inherit from the authenticated user's RBAC profile and calls are attributed to that user. Security documentation says only authenticated, active, licensed users with valid licenses can access data, and Outreach RBAC profile permissions apply. Revocation is described as IDP-controlled. No MCP-specific retention period or AI training statement was found in consulted pages.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Outreach says access to data is governed by the same user permissions as the web experience. Admins can enable or disable the server and configure create/delete availability. Developer docs describe structured response shapes and runtime-discoverable schemas.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: RBAC enforcement, OAuth authentication, admin server setting, and create/delete switches are described as server/product controls. Annotation-driven confirmations, client call logging, and client-side rate limits are recommendations to the agent runtime; the usage guide explicitly says the MCP server does not throttle or undo.

contradictions: The developer landing page says the Tool Catalog has 32 available tools, while the current official Tool Catalog page is titled "Tool Catalog (42 tools)" and divides them into 27 read/discovery, 13 write/mutation, and 2 schema tools.
The Tool Catalog says all tools advertise openWorldHint:false; the Tool Annotations page says all Outreach tools have openWorldHint:true.

The OAuth protected-resource metadata advertises only the scope prospects.all, while official documentation describes access across accounts, opportunities, sequences, tasks, meetings, users, and other data. The supplied evidence does not explain scope coverage.
The apis.io catalogue reports 41 tools (27 read, 11 write, 3 schema), differing from the official Tool Catalog's 42 (27 read, 13 write, 2 schema).
The Claude connector directory lists 14 tool names that differ from names in the official catalog. They are preserved as third-party entries in actions.json and are not treated as official names.
observations_for_research: The server combines read tools with record creation, batch enrollment/removal, deletes, and AI question-answer tools that create Q&A history records.
Delete availability is documented as off by default at the organization level, while create actions are on by default; the tool catalog still advertises these operations.
Official guidance explicitly places confirmation flows, client logging, and rate limiting in the client layer and says the MCP server does not throttle or undo.
The OAuth metadata's single advertised scope is broad in its apparent data coverage relative to the documented tool catalog; the mapping is not explained by available evidence.
notes: Checked the supplied links.json, pages/ copies including HTML and script extracts where present, links_check.txt, and code/GITHUB_COMMITS.txt. No official repository, package, endpoint tool manifest, or server source code was found; the endpoint's supplied OAuth metadata and HTTP 401 response were used as provided. Pricing details beyond the Amplify requirement were not found. Consulted third-party catalogues for cross-checking; Claude's directory is treated as third-party, and the apis.io count warning is reported as a discrepancy. Other unofficial/community server evidence was not used as evidence for the official endpoint.
